concepts.name: NVIDIA Infra Controller (NICo)
concepts.definition: NVIDIA's site controller software. It discovers bare-metal hosts through their BMCs, pairs them with their DPUs, provisions them and manages them as tenant infrastructure. It runs on a Kubernetes cluster.

concepts.name: NICo Core
concepts.definition: The core control plane of NICo, deployed as the 'nico' Helm release. It includes nico-api (a gRPC API) and the DHCP, DNS, PXE, NTP and SSH console services used to discover and provision hosts.

concepts.name: NICo REST
concepts.definition: The REST control plane that sits on top of NICo Core. It provides the REST API, workflow workers and site-manager, and it depends on Keycloak, Temporal and PostgreSQL. It lives in-tree under rest-api/.

concepts.name: NICo Flow
concepts.definition: A NICo component installed in setup Phase 7h. Its values can be overridden with --flow-values. The pages do not explain what it does.

concepts.name: setup.sh orchestrator
concepts.definition: The script in helm-prereqs/ that installs every prerequisite and NICo component in numbered phases (0 to 7i). Flags such as --skip-vault, --skip-dpf and -y control it. It is idempotent, so you upgrade by re-running it.

concepts.name: Preflight checks (preflight.sh)
concepts.definition: A validation script that runs at the start of setup.sh. It checks environment variables, required tools, MetalLB config, cluster reachability, node count, kernel parameters, DNS, registry connectivity and Vault-free values. Errors stop the setup.

concepts.name: Kubernetes cluster
concepts.definition: A container orchestration platform. NICo runs on a cluster you provide, which needs at least three schedulable nodes, working cluster DNS and certain kernel networking settings.

concepts.name: Kubernetes workload and config objects
concepts.definition: The basic Kubernetes resources the docs refer to constantly. Pods run containers. StatefulSets run replicated stateful apps. Secrets and ConfigMaps hold credentials and configuration. Jobs run one-off tasks. Services expose pods on the network.

concepts.name: Kubernetes Service types (LoadBalancer, NodePort, ClusterIP)
concepts.definition: The ways a Kubernetes Service can be exposed. ClusterIP is reachable only inside the cluster. NodePort opens a port on every node. LoadBalancer gets an external IP, which MetalLB supplies on bare metal.

concepts.name: Persistent storage (StorageClass, PVC, local-path-provisioner)
concepts.definition: The Kubernetes system for durable volumes. local-path-provisioner creates StorageClasses backed by node-local disks, and the PostgreSQL and Vault volume claims use them.

concepts.name: Helm and helmfile
concepts.definition: Helm is the Kubernetes package manager. It installs charts configured through YAML values files. helmfile declaratively manages several Helm releases and uses the helm-diff plugin to show what will change.

concepts.name: Kustomize
concepts.definition: A Kubernetes tool that customizes manifests by layering overlays on top of base manifests. setup.sh can apply a site overlay with it, and the REST stack uses kustomize bases.

concepts.name: Container image registry
concepts.definition: A server that stores container images. You push the NICo images you built to a registry, and the cluster pulls them from it. Authenticated registries such as NVIDIA NGC need an image pull secret.

concepts.name: Building NICo containers
concepts.definition: Compiling the NICo Core, DPU BFB artifact and admin CLI images from source on Ubuntu 24.04, including cross-compilation for x86_64 and aarch64, then pushing them to a registry.

concepts.name: BlueField-3 DPU
concepts.definition: An NVIDIA SmartNIC with its own Arm cores and operating system. It runs networking and isolation functions for its host. Before use it must be flashed with a BlueField firmware bundle and set to DPU operating mode.

concepts.name: DOCA Platform Framework (DPF)
concepts.definition: NVIDIA's Kubernetes-based framework for provisioning DPUs. It is NICo's default way to provision host DPUs and includes argo-cd, kamaji, NFD and the dpf-operator. You opt out with --skip-dpf or per host with dpf_enabled=false.

concepts.name: PXE / iPXE network boot
concepts.definition: Booting a machine over the network: it gets an address from DHCP, then downloads a boot image. NICo's nico-pxe service serves boot images. iPXE-based DPU provisioning is the deprecated alternative to DPF.

concepts.name: Baseboard Management Controller (BMC)
concepts.definition: A small embedded controller on a server that allows remote power control, monitoring and configuration independent of the host OS. NICo discovers hosts through their BMCs and replaces the factory credentials with site-wide ones.

concepts.name: Out-of-band (OOB) management network
concepts.definition: A separate management network that connects the BMCs. Its switches must relay BMC DHCP requests to the nico-dhcp VIP so that NICo can find the hosts.

concepts.name: Redfish API
concepts.definition: A standard REST API that BMCs expose for hardware management. NICo uses it to discover and control hosts.

concepts.name: DHCP and DHCP relay
concepts.definition: DHCP automatically assigns IP addresses and options, such as NTP servers, to machines on a network. A DHCP relay forwards DHCP requests from other network segments to a central server, here the Kea-based nico-dhcp service.

concepts.name: DNS and DNS records
concepts.definition: The system that maps names to IP addresses. NICo needs cluster DNS to work, external A records for its API and ingress hostnames, and it runs its own nico-dns and Unbound services.

concepts.name: NTP time synchronization
concepts.definition: A protocol for keeping clocks synchronized. NICo uses enterprise NTP servers to set BMC time before ingestion. It can also run a 3-replica chrony service (nico-ntp) whose addresses are handed to DPUs over DHCP.

concepts.name: Virtual IP address (VIP)
concepts.definition: A stable IP address assigned to a service rather than to one machine. Each NICo Core LoadBalancer service needs a fixed VIP from the MetalLB pool so that DHCP relays, DNS and PXE can be configured in advance.

concepts.name: MetalLB
concepts.definition: A load-balancer implementation for bare-metal Kubernetes. It assigns external IPs to LoadBalancer Services from configured IPAddressPools and announces them with either BGP or Layer 2.

concepts.name: BGP peering
concepts.definition: Border Gateway Protocol is a routing protocol in which peers exchange routes. MetalLB peers each node with its top-of-rack (TOR) switch, using a cluster ASN and a per-node TOR ASN, to advertise the VIPs.

concepts.name: Layer 2 advertisement (ARP)
concepts.definition: A MetalLB mode for flat networks without BGP. A node answers ARP requests for the VIP on the local network segment.

concepts.name: IP subnets and CIDR notation
concepts.definition: A notation such as 10.0.0.0/28 for writing IP address ranges. It is used throughout siteConfig and MetalLB pools for prefixes, gateways and deny lists.

concepts.name: VLAN
concepts.definition: A virtual LAN, which splits one physical Layer 2 network into isolated segments identified by a VLAN ID. NICo allocates VLAN IDs from a configured pool.

concepts.name: VXLAN and VNI
concepts.definition: An overlay technique that tunnels Layer 2 networks over a Layer 3 underlay. Each overlay network is identified by a VNI and handled at tunnel endpoints (VTEPs). NICo allocates VNIs from a pool and needs IPv4 VXLAN tunnel endpoints.

concepts.name: FNN (site fabric isolation)
concepts.definition: A NICo site networking mode that the pages use without defining. It uses site fabric prefixes and null routes (blackholes) to isolate instances, and it is required for IPv6-only admin networking.

concepts.name: siteConfig (site TOML configuration)
concepts.definition: A TOML block in nico-core.yaml that defines the site's identity, DHCP and NTP servers, fabric prefixes, deny prefixes, resource pools and initial networks.

concepts.name: NICo resource pools
concepts.definition: Ranges that NICo allocates from. They cover loopback IPs for hosts and DPUs, VLAN IDs and VXLAN VNIs. All three must be non-empty.

concepts.name: Admin and underlay networks
concepts.definition: Networks NICo creates at startup. The admin network carries host management traffic. Underlay data-plane networks are defined one per L3 segment. An IPv4 prefix needs a gateway.

concepts.name: TLS certificates and X.509 SAN
concepts.definition: Certificates that prove a server's identity and enable encrypted connections. Subject Alternative Names list the hostnames a certificate covers, and a wildcard covers exactly one DNS label.

concepts.name: Public key infrastructure and CA trust
concepts.definition: The system in which a Certificate Authority signs certificates and clients trust that CA. NICo bootstraps a private site CA, so clients must import its CA bundle before they accept the certificates it issues.

concepts.name: Mutual TLS (mTLS)
concepts.definition: TLS in which client and server both present certificates. NICo uses it between components such as Temporal, RMS and the site-agent's gRPC client.

concepts.name: cert-manager and Issuers
concepts.definition: A Kubernetes controller that issues and renews TLS certificates as Certificate resources. Issuers and cluster-wide ClusterIssuers define how certificates are signed, for example by the site CA or by Vault.

concepts.name: HashiCorp Vault
concepts.definition: A secrets manager. NICo installs it by default as a 3-node HA cluster with Raft storage. It stores credentials and issues certificates, and it must be initialized and unsealed. --skip-vault installs NICo without it.

concepts.name: Credential store (Vault vs Postgres)
concepts.definition: Where NICo keeps BMC and UEFI credentials. It is Vault by default, or PostgreSQL when the site is installed without Vault. In the Postgres case, certificates come from the site-issuer ClusterIssuer instead.

concepts.name: External Secrets Operator
concepts.definition: A Kubernetes operator that syncs secrets from external stores such as Vault into Kubernetes Secrets, using SecretStore and ClusterSecretStore resources.

concepts.name: KMIP KEK provider
concepts.definition: An opt-in feature that gets the key-encryption keys protecting stored secrets from an external KMIP key-management server. The connection uses client TLS files (ca.pem, client.pem, client.key).

concepts.name: Zalando postgres-operator (nico-pg-cluster)
concepts.definition: A Kubernetes operator that runs highly available PostgreSQL clusters. NICo uses it to run nico-pg-cluster, the shared database for Core, REST, the site-agent, Keycloak, Temporal and RMS.

concepts.name: Kubernetes Ingress and ingress controllers
concepts.definition: An Ingress routes external HTTP(S) traffic to Services by hostname, and an ingress controller such as Contour/Envoy or nginx handles it. You can use one to expose nico-rest-api on a domain name with TLS instead of a NodePort.

concepts.name: OpenID Connect (OIDC) and identity providers
concepts.definition: A standard for authentication built on OAuth 2.0. An identity provider issues signed tokens, and APIs validate them by checking the issuer and audience.

concepts.name: Keycloak
concepts.definition: An open-source identity provider that supports OIDC. setup.sh deploys a dev instance with a 'nico' realm and an 'ncx-service' client. You can point production at your own IdP instead.

concepts.name: OAuth2 client credentials flow and JWT bearer tokens
concepts.definition: A machine-to-machine flow in which a client exchanges its ID and secret for a signed JWT access token, then sends it in an Authorization: Bearer header. The token's iss claim must match what the API expects.

concepts.name: Temporal workflow engine
concepts.definition: A durable workflow orchestration system used by NICo REST. Each site's UUID becomes its Temporal namespace.

concepts.name: gRPC
concepts.definition: A remote procedure call framework that runs over HTTP/2. NICo Core exposes a gRPC API, which nico-admin-cli and the site-agent use.

concepts.name: NICo REST site-agent
concepts.definition: A StatefulSet that connects a site's NICo Core to NICo REST. A bootstrap Job registers it with site-manager using a one-time password, and it is then bound to the site UUID.

concepts.name: Site and site UUID registration
concepts.definition: Each NICo installation manages exactly one site, which has a stable UUID. setup.sh reuses, adopts or mints the UUID and registers the site automatically, so you must not create sites manually.

concepts.name: Org bootstrap (InfrastructureProvider, Tenant, TenantAccount)
concepts.definition: A one-time GET call to the REST API. It lazily creates the org's InfrastructureProvider, a Tenant, and a TenantAccount linking them. Site operations return 404 until it has been called.

concepts.name: nicocli
concepts.definition: The CLI for the NICo REST API, built from rest-api/. It is used for site management, org bootstrap and instance operations.

concepts.name: nico-admin-cli
concepts.definition: The CLI for the NICo Core gRPC API, built with cargo from crates/admin-cli. It is used for credentials, expected machines, TPM approval and host ingestion.

concepts.name: Site-wide BMC and UEFI credentials
concepts.definition: The BMC root password and the host and DPU UEFI passwords that NICo applies to machines after ingestion. All three must be set before Site Explorer will contact any BMC.

concepts.name: Expected machines manifest
concepts.definition: A JSON list of the hosts NICo should ingest. Each entry has the BMC MAC address, factory BMC credentials and chassis serial number, plus an optional dpf_enabled flag.

concepts.name: Site Explorer
concepts.definition: The NICo Core process that repeatedly finds BMCs on the network and explores them over Redfish to discover hosts. It fails with MissingCredentials until the site-wide credentials are set.

concepts.name: Measured Boot with TPM 2.0
concepts.definition: A Trusted Platform Module records hashes of boot components in PCR registers. NICo compares these measurements to approved values to establish a machine's cryptographic identity before ingestion.

concepts.name: Host ingestion
concepts.definition: The process in which NICo discovers a host via Redfish, pairs it with its DPUs, provisions the DPUs and brings the host to a ready state.

concepts.name: Rack Management Service (RMS)
concepts.definition: A NICo service installed by default in Phase 5c. It uses mTLS and an rms database on nico-pg-cluster, and you opt out with --skip-rms. The pages do not describe its function in detail.

concepts.name: Upgrade and teardown
concepts.definition: To upgrade, re-run setup.sh with new image tags; it preserves Vault, Postgres, MetalLB config and the site UUID. clean.sh removes all NICo components, namespaces and released volumes.
